*   **Member Name:** Quinn Ellison
*   **Member ID:** W391580594
*   **Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), State of Montana
*   **Reference Number:** POC-DF42BEB029-97975
*   **Requested Service:** Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446 - Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty)
*   **Ordering Surgeon:** Dr. Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery
*   **Denial Date:** August 4, 2026
*   **Appeals Deadline:** January 31, 2027

To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing to formally appeal Aetna's denial of the prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) on my [left/right] knee, to be performed by Dr. Lindqvist. The denial letter dated August 4, 2026, states: "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." 

This determination is incorrect. My clinical records and objective imaging studies fully satisfy Aetna’s medical necessity criteria outlined in Clinical Policy Bulletin (CPB) #0660: "Knee Arthroplasty". Below, I demonstrate how my medical history and specific diagnostic imaging align directly with Aetna's guidelines.

### 1. Direct Refutation of the Denial Reason: Objective Imaging Findings
The sole basis of your denial is the assertion that my imaging does not support medical necessity. However, Aetna’s CPB #0660 states that unicompartmental knee arthroplasty is considered medically necessary when there is:
> "Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) (see Appendix) affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint"

**My Medical Records:**
*   **MRI of the [left/right] knee dated May 28, 2026,** explicitly demonstrates **"full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition"** and confirms **"Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially."** 
*   This objective, advanced degenerative change is localized strictly to a single compartment (the medial compartment), which meets the exact standard of radiographic evidence of severe single-compartment osteoarthritis required by your policy.

### 2. Clinical and Functional Presentation (ADL Interference)
Aetna’s CPB #0660 requires that the patient present with:
> "Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint"

**My Medical Records:**
*   I have suffered from **18 months of progressive, severe pain** in my [left/right] knee, which is completely unrelieved by rest.
*   This pain severely limits my activities of daily living (ADLs). Specifically, my records document that I **cannot climb stairs without assistance** and **wake 3–4 times nightly with severe pain**, causing significant sleep deprivation.

### 3. Physical Examination Findings
Aetna's CPB #0660 requires:
> "Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination"

**My Medical Records:**
*   Dr. Lindqvist’s clinical examination documents that my **range of motion is significantly limited by pain** on the affected side.
*   The exam also notes **positive provocative testing** on my [left/right] knee, confirming joint line pathology consistent with severe medial compartment osteoarthritis.

### 4. History of Exhaustive Conservative Therapy
Aetna's CPB #0660 requires:
> "History of of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record... with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy)."

**My Medical Records:**
*   **Formal Physical Therapy:** I completed **16 weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy** from February 25, 2026, to June 17, 2026, totaling **24 visits**. This therapy was directed by a licensed physical therapist and focused specifically on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. My lack of improvement and ongoing functional deficits are fully documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
*   **Pharmacotherapy:** I have consistently taken **oral NSAIDs for 8 months** with inadequate relief of pain and zero functional improvement.
*   **Therapeutic Injection:** I received an intra-articular **corticosteroid injection on May 2, 2026**, which provided only 4 weeks of partial, temporary relief before my symptoms returned to baseline.

### 5. Absence of Contraindications
Aetna's CPB #0660 notes relative and absolute contraindications. My medical history rules out all exclusions:
*   **Corticosteroid timing:** The policy excludes coverage if there is a "Corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty". My last injection was on May 2, 2026. Any upcoming scheduled surgery date will occur well past the 12-week safety window.
*   **Body Mass Index (BMI):** My BMI is **29**, which is well below Aetna's relative contraindication threshold of a BMI greater than 40.
*   **Other Factors:** I am a non-smoker, have no active joint or systemic infections, no untreated substance use, and have intact, stable ligaments (including the ACL) confirmed on my May 2026 MRI.

### Conclusion
The clinical and radiographic data submitted by Dr. Lindqvist's office paint a clear picture of a patient with severe, bone-on-bone (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4) osteoarthritis restricted to the medial compartment of the [left/right] knee. I have exhausted more than 4 months of formal, in-person physical therapy, oral anti-inflammatories, and steroid injections, and yet my pain remains so severe that I cannot walk up stairs independently or sleep through the night. 

I meet every single standard outlined in Aetna's "Knee Arthroplasty" policy. I request that you immediately reverse this denial and approve the requested unicompartmental knee replacement so that I can proceed with surgery. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Quinn Ellison
